siblings.title: The 2026 React Router Landscape: TanStack Router vs React Router vs Wouter vs Next.js
siblings.summary: For a client-rendered React 19 admin SPA, TanStack Router is the sharpest fit and React Router the safest default; Wouter is for simple apps and Next.js App Router is the wrong grain.

siblings.title: Type-Safe Routing & Typed Search-Param State in React (2026)
siblings.summary: TanStack Router is the only router with typed, schema-validated search-param state end to end — the decisive edge for a filter-heavy admin console, at the cost of advanced-type complexity.

siblings.title: Library-mode router vs meta-framework (and RSC) for a React 19 admin SPA in 2026
siblings.summary: For an auth-gated internal admin SPA, a standalone router on Vite is still a first-class 2026 choice; RSC and meta-frameworks solve problems this app doesn't have.

siblings.title: Migration Effort & Lock-In: Choosing a React Router in 2026
siblings.summary: Already on React Router? Staying is near-drop-in. Greenfield SPA? The lock-in and churn math tilts toward TanStack Router.

sources.title: React Router — Data Loading (framework)
sources.claim: React Router v7 loaders/clientLoader fetch route data before render and actions auto-revalidate all loaders after a mutation.

sources.title: TanStack Router — Data Loading guide
sources.claim: TanStack Router's built-in cache suits apps sharing little data between routes but has no shared caching/deduping and no built-in mutation APIs.

sources.title: TkDodo — TanStack Router and Query
sources.claim: When using TanStack Query, disable the router's cache so one player owns caching; treat loaders as fire-and-forget priming and read via useSuspenseQuery.

sources.title: TanStack Router — Query integration
sources.claim: The TanStack Query integration automates SSR dehydration/hydration and streaming between router and query.

sources.title: master.dev — TanStack Router data loading (part 2)
sources.claim: Loaders prefetch via queryClient, useSuspenseQuery reads it, dedup latches onto one request, and useDeferredValue avoids waterfalls.

sources.title: react-router discussion #14037
sources.claim: For CSR-only apps TanStack Query alone works without framework mode; running both loaders and Query in parallel is an anti-pattern.

sources.title: React Router — Race Conditions
sources.claim: React Router cancels interrupted in-flight requests and commits only fresh revalidation responses, but backend integrity is out of scope.

sources.title: react-router issue #10473
sources.claim: Fetcher revalidation still has documented race-condition edge cases.

sources.title: The Road to Enterprise — RTK Query vs TanStack Query
sources.claim: RTK Query and TanStack Query solve the same caching/dedup/refetch problems; RTK Query's tag system auto-refetches related queries after a mutation.

sources.title: @rtk-query/codegen-openapi (npm)
sources.claim: RTK Query ships an official OpenAPI code generator producing fully-typed endpoints from a spec.

sources.title: byteiota — TanStack 2026
sources.claim: By early 2026 TanStack Query reached roughly 12 million weekly npm downloads.

sources.title: programmingarehard — Contributing to React Router
sources.claim: React Router v7 re-runs loaders by default after mutations, requiring shouldRevalidate/callsite opt-out to prevent unwanted refetches.
